title: The Panama Canal Lifts Giant Ships 85 Feet With No Pumps

scenes.text: Ships climb 85 feet without a single pump.
That's how the Panama Canal works. Ships ride water uphill.
Water from a lake flows by gravity into huge concrete chambers.
Each chamber takes about 26 million gallons, and fills in under ten minutes.
A full trip uses around 52 million gallons of fresh water.
No engines push the water. Gravity does all the lifting.

description:
Ships climb 85 feet without a single pump.
The Panama Canal lets gravity do the work: lake water flows into huge locks, and each chamber fills in under ten minutes with roughly 26 million gallons.
Would you want to take a ship through?
first_comment: Gravity does all the lifting. What is your favorite piece of engineering?
